data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 makes a boundary-edge argument for the panel but never supplies the evidence test the problem explicitly demands: what evidence within a single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain from checklist compliance that merely tracks the right answer. Its mechanism says the checklist forces slow review and flags boundary triggers, but a checklist that mechanically flags boundary triggers can still be mere compliance tracking the correct answer; flagging behavior alone does not separate genuine gain from rote adherence. The counterconditions (insufficient training, coarse checklist) describe failure modes, not an evidential discriminator. The claim and mechanism therefore fail to address the second, evidence-identification requirement of the problem.
